rationale: Added the operand the last interpretation named, and the draft-side run shows the provenance of the rejected change. Each rejection event now carries log_types, the type of the entries from the node's first index up to its committed index: for all three rejections at seed 35 the log is '1:t0 2:t2 3:t0 4:t2' - a normal entry, a ConfChangeV2, a normal entry, and the rejected ConfChangeV2 at index 4. In EntryType terms that is normal, ConfChangeV2, normal, ConfChangeV2, i.e. the node consumed two joint-entering configuration entries with no leave-joint entry between them (the only entry between them is normal, which is what a propose-time rewrite to a normal entry produces), while applied_before=3 for nodes 3 and 1 and 0 for the rebuilt node 4 and reapplied_entry=false in all three. Combined with the earlier receipt's operands this says the harness applied committed entries in order and the log itself carried a second joint-entering change behind an unapplied first one, which is exactly the shape the propose-time guard is supposed to prevent by consulting the leader's own applied configuration and tracker. I am not asserting the defect from a draft-side run: the experiment below requests isolated execution of these bytes so the log_types operands are receipt-backed, after which the interpretation can state what the log supports about the guard's reach.

scope.description: Fourteenth revision of the same fixed harness; probes A-C and the deterministic joint-change case are unchanged. The sweep keeps configuration targets, application lag, joint transitions, restarts, the liveness witness and the recovered apply guard, and the first three rejections now also report log_types - the (index, EntryType) of the node's entries from its first index up to its committed index, capped at eight entries - alongside applied_before, applying_before, reapplied_entry, entry index/term/change count/joint flag and the node state. invariant_sweep_summary still reports all counters including invalid_change_applies and invalid_change_reasons.
assumptions: Everything comes from the snapshot's own facilities (newTestRaft, newTestMemoryStorage, newNetwork, nextEnts, confChangeToMsg, applyConfChange, hasUnappliedConfChanges, promotable, newRaft, SetHardState, raftLog.slice); no production logic is modified.

log_types is read at rejection time from the rejecting node's own log for the range [firstIndex, committed], capped at eight entries, and reports EntryType values only - it does not report which change each ConfChangeV2 entry carries.
The operands still do not report the proposer's tracker or applied index at the moment the entry was appended, so they constrain the log but not the guard evaluation directly.
Randomness is fixed per seed; counts are descriptive, not rates.

experiment.prefix: For each of 60 seeds: build nodes 1..4 with newTestRaft(id,10,1,newTestMemoryStorage(withPeers(1,2,3))); nt := newNetwork(nodes[1],nodes[2],nodes[3]) then nt.peers[4] = nodes[4]. For 60 steps pick one of MsgHup, MsgProp, tick(), isolate, recover, TransferLeader, a ConfChangeV2 proposal on the leader (single change, target drawn from node 4 or a non-leader member, half the time JointImplicit), a restart of a random node, or persist/apply of all nodes; after each step persist/apply nodes 1..4 (skipping one node about one time in six; capturing applied_before/applying_before; applying committed conf changes under recover and, for the first three rejections, emitting invalid_change_apply with entry operands, node state, applied/applying before, reapplied_entry and log_types), then evaluate the four invariants and the liveness witness, finally emitting invariant_sweep_summary.
experiment.revision_reason: Same investigation and sweep case as the previous execution, with log_types added to the rejection operands so the entry sequence at the rejecting node is observable. A draft-side run reported log_types='1:t0 2:t2 3:t0 4:t2' for all three rejections, i.e. normal, ConfChangeV2, normal, ConfChangeV2 with no leave entry between the two configuration entries, which is construction feedback only and is why isolated execution is requested.
